name: Eden
subcategory: workplace ops, desk and room booking
tagline: Workplace operations software for offices: desk booking, room scheduling, visitor check-in and internal ticketing in one admin console.

pricing.basis: typically per desk or per employee per month, module based
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Strip Eden down and the core is a booking database: desks, rooms, time slots, one row per reservation, plus a log of who walked in the front door. An agent will hand you a working desk and room booker with a clickable floor grid in an afternoon, and for a ten person office that is genuinely enough. What breaks is everything around the edges: two way Google and Outlook calendar sync, SSO, the Slack bot people actually book from, the iPad kiosk with badge printing, and the reports someone in finance wants before renewing the lease. None of that is impossible, it is just a long tail of OAuth scopes and hardware quirks that eats the weekend and then keeps eating. Build it if you own the office and the office is small; buy it if you have offices, plural.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where a small team books desks and meeting rooms from a floor grid and calendar view, with a visitor sign-in log and simple usage reporting.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine or cheap VPS to run it on
A shared floor plan you are willing to represent as a grid of labeled desks
Optional SMTP credentials in .env if you want booking confirmation emails
whatYouLose: Two way calendar sync, so room bookings will not appear in Google or Outlook without real OAuth work
The Slack and Teams bots that make booking a one line habit instead of a website visit
Visitor kiosk mode, badge printing and NDA capture on an iPad in the lobby
SSO, SCIM directory sync and audit trails that IT will ask about
Native mobile apps, plus someone else worrying about uptime when 40 people try to book Monday at 9am
moatNotes: The booking logic is trivial. The value is being the thing already wired into the calendar, the badge printer and the office manager's routine.
whyPeopleStillPay: Facilities software is bought by one person to stop a recurring argument, and the price is rounding error against rent. The buyer is not comparing feature lists, they are comparing a vendor with a support inbox against maintaining an internal app that breaks the week they are on holiday. Add the fact that visitor logs and badge policies often live inside a security or compliance checklist, and the case for self-hosting a weekend build in a real company gets thin fast. For a single small office with no compliance story, the calculus flips.
notes: The booking app is a Saturday. The calendar sync, kiosk hardware and IT review are the actual product.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted office operations app called Deskly. Single stack, no menus: Next.js 15 (App Router, TypeScript), Tailwind, SQLite via better-sqlite3, Drizzle ORM, deployed as a plain Node process.

Data model:
- offices (name, timezone)
- desks (office, label, zone, x and y grid coords, active flag)
- rooms (office, name, capacity, amenities as text)
- bookings (resource type desk or room, resource id, user id, start, end, note)
- users (name, email, role member or admin)
- visitors (name, company, host user id, signed in at, signed out at)

Features in scope:
1. Desk booking: a clickable floor grid rendered from desk x and y coords, colored free, booked, mine. Pick a date, click a desk, book for the day or a half day. Conflicts rejected at the database level with a unique constraint plus an overlap check.
2. Room booking: day view timeline per room, 30 minute slots, drag or click to book, capacity shown.
3. My bookings page with cancel.
4. Visitor log: a /kiosk route in large touch friendly type where a guest types name, company and host, which writes a visitor row and shows a confirmation. Admin can sign visitors out.
5. Admin: CRUD for offices, desks, rooms and users, plus a usage page showing desk utilization percent and top booked rooms for the last 30 days, with CSV export.
6. Seed script that creates one office, 24 desks in a 6x4 grid, 3 rooms and 5 users.

Out of scope, do not build and do not stub with fake UI: Google or Outlook calendar sync, Slack or Teams bots, SSO or SAML, badge printing, payments, native mobile apps, analytics or telemetry of any kind.

Auth: single shared password from ADMIN_PASSWORD in .env for admin routes, plus a simple name picker cookie for member identity. No accounts, no email verification. If SMTP_URL is present in .env, send booking confirmation emails; if absent, log them to stdout and carry on.

Deliver: working app, seeded database, npm run dev and npm run start, a README with setup in under ten lines, and a .env.example. Mobile responsive layout, keyboard accessible grid. No placeholder TODOs in shipped code.
